title: A real-world study on the subjectively perceived effectiveness, use and acceptance of digital health applications in the treatment of insomnia within routine outpatient sleep medicine practice
summary: Digital health applications for the treatment of sleep problems are increasingly being used in healthcare. However, little is currently known about how these services are used in everyday life and accepted by patients, or whether, from their perspective, they contribute to an improvement in sleep. The aim of the study is therefore to investigate the use, acceptance and perceived benefits of digital health applications for the treatment of chronic insomnia (difficulty falling asleep and/or staying asleep) in outpatient sleep medicine. The focus is particularly on patients´ personal experiences and assessments.

interventions.name: Patients diagnosed with chronic insomnia are provided a digital health app and are asked to complete questionnaires on the subjectively perceived effectiveness of the treatment, both before and after the end of the therapy.
